item.title: Reciprocal connections dynamically build consensus between neocortical areas
item.headline: How two mouse visual areas settle into agreement
item.authors: Mitra Javadzadeh, Marine Schimel, Sonja B. Hofer, Yashar Ahmadian and Guillaume Hennequin
item.summary: Reanalyzed mouse recordings support models in which communication between visual areas sustains matching activity patterns. A simple visual task cannot establish a general explanation of consciousness.

evidence.question: How do visual areas coordinate their activity?
evidence.method: Existing recordings and light-based neural suppression; circuit models fitted to seven mice, timing analyses using twelve.
evidence.limitations: Two mouse areas; sensory, movement, and reward signals overlap.

explainer.finding: Matching activity patterns persisted longer than conflicting ones, as the circuit models predicted.
explainer.method: Researchers reanalyzed simultaneous V1 and LM recordings during a rewarded tilted-stripe task, including brief suppression of either area.
explainer.meaning: Think of recognizing a stripe's tilt: feedback could help separate areas maintain a consistent interpretation.
explainer.limits: This mechanism remains model-dependent. Broader brain functions and human subjective experience were not tested.
